quest.title: The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose
quest.description: Paimon is a bit worried about Adeptus Fujin's condition. If you have time, it might be good to pay another visit to Chiwang Terrace.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

talks.objective: Ascend the summit of Mt. Laixin

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon. You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Lingyuan? Why are you over here?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Because I can't get in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't get in? Uh, where can't you get into?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Carp's Rest. Where Fujin is resting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Carp's Rest... Oh! You mean the place Fujin dragged us off to way back when?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: It is an abode sealed by her adeptal energy. I don't have her adeptal energy. Thus, I cannot go to her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But you didn't mention anything before she went back to rest...

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: It escaped my mind.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The adeptal energy you possess is sufficient to open the gate of Carp's Rest. So yes, I need your help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a sec, so you've been waiting here for us this whole time?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I was not waiting for you. I was looking for a way into Carp's Rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That seems like pretty much the same thing to... Uh, anyway, we're a bit worried about Fujin's condition too, so why don't we go see her together?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Fine. Thank you both.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, how could you forget something as important as that!? Really, now.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: It is because I am a slow-witted beast. Seeing her, I think of many things, and forget many things. It is my fault.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The adeptal energy you possess is sufficient to open the gate of Carp's Rest. So yes, I need your help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, this should be your abode, right, Fujin? It feels a bit different from the other adeptal abodes we've been in... How should Paimon put it... it feels more... pragmatic?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are no weird mechanisms or transparent floating bridges...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: I am very sorry... I was just too embarrassed before, and so never explained clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: I cannot create new adeptal realms like the adepti of the south. "Carp's Rest" is no "abode." At best, it's just a "cave"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cave, realm, whatever! They're all "abodes" where adepti live, aren't they? Still, we don't even know when you can turn back into your human form...

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: All the power she accumulated has dispersed across this land. She will be unable to revert to human form for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I am the same way when I've exhausted my power. After Master died, the snow fell, melted, and then it fell once more after melting, and did so countless times before I could regain human form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's it... huh? Wait a sec, Lingyuan, you can turn into a person too!?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Why, of course! There is much you two know not! Why, back then, on Mt. Yaojun, Lingyuan's looks were—

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Fujin. No need to speak of such things. It has nothing to do with the present topic.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Eh? So, the whole thing about eating too many teacakes at the temple fair in human form, and crying to Herblord about brewing weight-loss tea...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Or the incident where you accidentally drank the celebratory libations and hauled forest boars in to ask them "Who's prettier, me or Herblord?"... Ah! But I needn't speak of such things after all, do I?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: ...Fujin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! After all that, Paimon's getting curious. What does your human form look like, Lingyuan? Would you be as blue as you are now? Or would you be... Uh, a slightly lighter shade?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I do not understand your curiosity. You are people too. If you are interested in human forms, just look at yourselves.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Hehe... Anyway, thank you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I never imagined the day would come when I would be able to talk to others like this...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: *cough*— As one has found oneself in such a joyous state of mind, one is willing to bestow protection upon you two for your journey, guaranteeing success and great fortune...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...Sorry, I got a bit carried away. I wanted to try being like those adepti, so I thought I'd try out a phrase or two...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Anyway! I'll be staying here and praying for your journey to go smoothly.

choices.text: Lingyuan, could you turn human, just for a second?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I refuse. Human bodies are weak. They lack fangs to rend and rip prey, and claws to hound and hunt enemies. I would not do such a thing unless commanded to by Fujin.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...Eh? R—Really? I—In that case, I think maybe we should just respect Lingyuan's wishes...?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I do not have any wishes. If you have some, tell me so directly.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin's Voice
dialogues.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Lingyuan... Why did you all come here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's Fujin's voice! And it's... coming from down below?

choices.text: I'm a little worried about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We're all worried about your health, so we just came here without giving you a heads up — you did the same thing to us first, so Paimon thinks we're square now!

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Huh? Ah! Sorry! When I returned here to rest, I think I forgot to unlock the entrance...! I am so sorry. You came here to see me, but I made things harder for you instead...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it wasn't much of a hassle! But why are you... uh, hiding in a puddle?

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Hmm, how should I put it...? Because I can't return to the form I prefer yet, and with you guys always seeing me in my Carp form, I can't help but feel a bit... embarrassed...

choices.text: You are aware that we've already seen it many, many times, right?

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Ahaha... But before, I could turn back into human form whenever I wanted, so I thought moving around as a Carp was just a matter of convenience. But now, all I have is this slick and slippery self, so I find it a bit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's a bit of a strange thing to be so insistent about... But anyway, all that matters is that you're okay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Lingyuan said that your adeptal energy wasn't consumed, it was just dispersed around the mountains, forests, and rivers of Chenyu Vale, and that's why you've been weakened so much...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we were to collect the scattered adeptal energy, just like when we were finding the Golden Carp in Yaodie Valley, then you'd get better, right?

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Yes... At least, in theory, that's correct, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, right? So if we see similar Carp, we should just bring them back here! That way, you'll recover much faster!

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Th—That would be far too much trouble for you! My power is not yet that feeble. If I simply rest here for some time, it will be enough...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's not that much of a hassle...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...We'll just keep our eyes peeled if we run into any.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Thank you, then. However, I really don't want to trouble you anymore on my behalf. You've already done so much for me.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: If the two of you should happen to find any more adeptal energy during your travels, please simply transfer it into the jade here.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Though balance has been restored to the water and soil, if we can add more power to the Rainjade, we can ensure favorable weather and prosperous years to come.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...And what about you?

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Really now! I already told you, all I need to do is rest here for a bit!

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I really am quite grateful, and quite happy, that you came to visit me. This is the first time anyone has come here since Herblord left.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: And thank you as well, Lingyuan.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I have done nothing worthy of your thanks.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: #Alright, enough of that! Then just think of it as me thanking you for bringing {NICKNAME} and Paimon here! Really, now...

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: #And lastly... Let me say thank you once more, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. For all you have done.

choices.text: So there's no need to hide yourself, is there?
Lingyuan is a little worried about you.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I am not. I just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Lingyuan's been so worried about your health that she can barely speak, so we just came here without giving you a heads up — but you did the same thing to us first, so Paimon thinks we're square now!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Bluey, Bluey, you didn't tell me the ending to that story you were telling me last time!

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Yes. I remember. However, I've changed my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: "Changed your mind"? What's that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I'll leave the ending of the story... to you.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Ehhh!? C'mon, Bluey, that's cheating! You promised that you'd tell me a story if I told you one! How come I'm the one telling both stories now!?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I'm just a simple-minded beast. I cannot think of a good ending.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: The ending I came up with was a bad ending. The story is also a bad story that wouldn't make anyone happy. So, I'll let you tell the ending of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: But that's still cheating!

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I do not deny that. As compensation, I can take you to see the hidden sights of Mt. Lingmeng.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Don't make that face. I will give you special permission to... Sit on my back, for five minutes or so. Ten minutes will do, too.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: In... In that case, then it's a deal! I'll think of an ending for the story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Lingyuan, is that you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry! Are you hunting? Did we disturb you?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I was not hunting. You did not disturb me either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Then were you just... spacing out? Like, thinking about tasty food and stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I wasn't thinking about you either. I was just thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thinking... Hang on, wait! What did you mean by that first part!?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: #I am thinking about the question {NICKNAME} asked before.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: "If human activities are part of the laws of nature, how would you view humanity?"

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: It has been too long since I last had contact with the humans constituting the settlement — I have not been there since Fujin and the snake left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you're making it sound like Little Mao doesn't count as a human!

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: #Little Mao is a human that belongs to the settled humans, but is not a human who constitutes the settlement. You and {NICKNAME} "constitute" travel companions, but you do not "belong" to {NICKNAME}. That is the difference.

choices.text: You don't consider Little Mao a part of the social order?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Not in full. Most human young are like this until they are completely absorbed by the order, just as it is in nature.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: It has been too long since I have been in contact with the humans who constitute the settlement. It could be because of hatred, fear, or maybe even both.

choices.text: Because they have encroached on the land that belongs to nature?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I don't know.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Or perhaps no obvious differences exist that separate "us" from "them," but I cannot be sure.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The young of the humans walk with me. Similarly, a youngling of our kin walks with a human out of curiosity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? A youngling of your kind?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: That child encountered a mortal in the mountains.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: So, I still cannot answer your question. I must continue to observe humanity.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: There are many things I do not understand. I will try to understand until I can answer your question, as I promised to.

choices.text: Because Fujin chose to sacrifice herself for them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't say weird things like that!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Listening to Mountain, it sounds like Fontaine's operas are pretty similar to ours!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Knights, magicians, brave warriors, and evil dragons, you kill me, I kill you, and in the end, everyone's dead!

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: What's important isn't the ending! It's the process — how you get there! Not every tragedy can be seen as a mere sequence of fight scenes!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Oh, oh! And the "Ray-more-young Golems" Mountain was just talking about sound really, really cool too! I wonder if they're bigger than Bluey?

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Eh? Bluey?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Oh, right! I never told you about Bluey, did I... How about this? You tell me more about "Ray-more-young Golems," and I'll tell you about Bluey!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Lingyuan? You keep staring at me. Do I have food on my face or something?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I was just thinking... No. It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Even if you and the snake both asked me to, I will never again take human form.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Hehe. I haven't ever asked you to before, have I now?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: ...Forget it. Let's go. Or did you not clamor to see the present tea garden?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Big Sis Fujin! Congratulations on returning to your former self!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Bluey already told me all about it! You really like tea, so I specially requested that Grandpa Lu make you a super-duper delicious teacake!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: That's right, I'm back, completely and totally back! Little Mao, thank you so much for preparing a teacake just for me, I'm so happy!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: There's some for you two, too! We can all eat teacakes together and celebrate Fujin's recovery!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, thanks, Little Mao! Since there's so much left, Paimon will take two pieces!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, thanks, Little Mao! Since that's the case, Paimon will take two... too? Waaah! There's only one piece left!
